name: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Saguaro, dune rodents and the rain that drives a volcanic desert.

tip.title: Take away the rain
tip.text: Desert plants only grow when rain arrives. Set Rainfall to -100% and watch the saguaro and grasses, then the herbivores, then coyotes and bobcats.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Intense desert sunshine drives growth for every plant, but only where rain or stored water allows it.
Scarce, irregular rain in this part of the Sonoran Desert decides when plants grow, flower and set seed. Saguaro growth tracks rainfall closely.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & detritivores
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the thin desert soil.
Giant columnar cactus that stores rainwater. Its fruit feeds doves and ants, bats pollinate its flowers, and woodpeckers carve nest holes that other birds reuse.
Evergreen shrub that dominates much of the desert flats and hosts many specialised insects.

nodes.name: White brittlebush
nodes.desc: Silvery shrub with yellow flowers. GloBI has the master blister beetle recorded feeding on it.
Wild sheep of the rocky peaks and cliffs. GloBI records it eating desert plants including a hedgehog cactus.
Endangered desert subspecies that eats mostly grasses and shrubs and copes with long spells without water.
Large desert hare that browses grasses and shrubs and is prey for most of the area's carnivores.
Sand-dune rodent that eats mostly seeds and gets most of its water from metabolism. Prey for coyotes, bobcats and snakes.
Rodent that builds den middens and feeds on cacti and other desert plants.
Large bat that hunts big arthropods such as beetles and scorpions, often taken on or near the ground.
Small rattlesnake of loose sand that ambushes lizards and small rodents such as kangaroo rats.
Nocturnal raptor that takes rodents and rabbits across deserts.
Soaring scavenger that finds carrion by smell and sight over open desert.
Adaptable top predator. GloBI records it taking pronghorn, bighorn, jackrabbits, woodrats and kangaroo rats.
Solitary cat of rocky desert and scrub that hunts rabbits, rodents and occasionally young pronghorn.
